title: Connected scheme with algebraically closed residue-field point is geometrically connected
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $X$ a connected scheme over $k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-scheme-over-base, def-weil-connected-scheme], so each residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is a field extension of $k$ through the structure morphism. If $X$ has a point $x$ such that $k$ is algebraically closed in $\kappa(x)$, i.e. every element of $\kappa(x)$ algebraic over $k$ lies in $k$, then $X$ is geometrically connected over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]: $X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ is connected for every field extension $K/k$.

proof.text: Let $T=\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(x))$ and let $T\to X$ be the canonical morphism associated to the point $x$. The hypothesis that $k$ is algebraically closed in $\kappa(x)$ is exactly the hypothesis of [lem-zl-field-extension-algebraically-closed-geometric], applied to the field extension $\kappa(x)/k$; hence $T$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$. After every field extension of $k$, the base change of $T$ is irreducible and therefore connected by [lem-pc-irreducible-space-connected]. Unfolding geometric connectedness in [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] shows that $T$ is geometrically connected over $k$.

source.place: Tag 04KV, proof: set T = Spec(kappa(x)); the hypothesis makes T geometrically irreducible, hence geometrically connected.

proof.text: The morphism $T\to X$ is a morphism of schemes over $k$, $X$ is connected by hypothesis, and $T$ is geometrically connected by Step 1. Apply the connected-point criterion [lem-trf-geometrically-connected-image-criterion] (Stacks Tag 056R) to conclude that $X$ is geometrically connected over $k$.
